- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative (no positive sentiment in history).
- Underestimate sharp upward moves in the first 5–7 days after a price spike; model tends to lag or underestimate momentum.
- Overshoot after initial spikes — model often peaks too high and then corrects downward, especially in 10–15 day windows.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently overcorrects downward after strong upward moves, then undercorrects later.
- When sentiment turns positive (even slightly, e.g., 0.25), model should adjust upward, but often fails to do so until later in the horizon.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to underestimating late-period volatility, especially after 20–25 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — model often ignores recent low prices when sentiment is flat, leading to underestimation.
